solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Digging implement boy singles out, unreasonably?

parts.note: a pick is a tool for breaking up ground
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A lad with a spade picks people out for no good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick on someone is to target or victimise them unfairly, singling them out for harsh treatment.

clue.text: Pelagia, losing energy, rides, strangely lifted

indicators.note: losing means the name Pelagia drops a letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: strangely suggests the letters of rides are set out oddly

explanation.surface: Pelagia, out of steam, rides off into an odd scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns RIDES into RISED. Pelagia is the heroine of Captain Corelli's Mandolin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifted can mean stolen, and plagiarised writing is lifted from another author: synonym.

clue.text: Military officer to beat volunteers with it

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve
in means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: An officer tries to beat his volunteers into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned army rank, an example of an officer; Captain Corelli again.

clue.text: Sort limbo dancing in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters of sort limbo jig about into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of limbo dance done on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is a volcanic island off Sicily, an example.

clue.text: No good hiding old African dictator's designation

indicators.note: hiding means the abbreviation for no good encloses the dictator's name

parts.note: Idi Amin was the ruler of Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A useless effort to conceal a dictator's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming is giving something a name, a designation, which makes it a synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers crazy, writing off leader

indicators.note: writing off the leader means the first letter of the word for crazy is dropped

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A report that some troops have gone mad, with their commander out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: BARMY is everyday British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a body of soldiers, a collective synonym.

clue.text: Bristles angrily when nagged, first of all

definitions.note: a plural clue word for a singular noun; the plural form would add an S

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone bristles angrily at being nagged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristles' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is a stiff bristle on grasses such as barley, a botanical synonym.

clue.text: I wound up in US resort

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the words I and the verb for wound are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to maim is to wound

explanation.surface: Someone ends up at an American holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like ended; 'wound' is MAIM and 'up' reverses I MAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a resort city in Florida, an example.

clue.text: According to head of advertising, salesmen returned

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word advertising is taken
returned means the word for salesmen is read backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives

explanation.surface: Someone cites the head of advertising on salesmen coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock synonym meaning in accordance with, as in instructions followed exactly.

clue.text: Mandras repaired roof

indicators.note: repaired suggests the letters of Mandras are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Mandras has fixed a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansard is a style of roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steep; an example.

clue.text: Record Republican amended proved to be wrong

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
edited means amended

explanation.surface: A Republican's record was revised after being shown false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' looks like an anagram signal but is EDITED.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory discredited has been shown false and so lost its credibility, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl of 14

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the girl is found inside that other entry

parts.note: 14 refers to the answer of 14-across, a word meaning in the sky

explanation.surface: A girl aged fourteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of 14' looks like an age; it points to the solution at 14-across, which hides the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is a female first name, a crossword staple for a girl.

clue.text: Instruments musician initially on island played

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of musician is taken
played suggests the letters of on island are performed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A musician first plays instruments on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Corelli's Mandolin is the novel that gives this setter a pseudonym and the puzzle its theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandolins are small stringed instruments of the lute family, an example.

clue.text: Map-reader who runs east, always

parts.note: the Orient is the East
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A map-reader who always heads east.
explanation.definitionFit: An orienteer races across country with a map and compass, a description of the sport's competitor.

clue.text: Organised party, married, in no particular order

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective describing arrangement without pattern

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so ran is organised
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An organised party leads to a wedding, oddly in no order at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Random arrangement is haphazard, without method or sequence, a synonym.

clue.text: Note prosecutor, Irish, involved in sort of collision?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a word that describes a kind of crash

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A prosecutor and an Irishman are caught up in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A midair collision is aircraft crashing in flight; the word qualifies that type, hence the question mark.

clue.text: In Hunstanton I organised The Merchant of Venice

indicators.note: In signals the name lies within the run of words Hunstanton I organised

explanation.surface: Someone staged the Shakespeare play in a Norfolk seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunstanton is a seaside resort in Norfolk. The play's title refers to Antonio, not Shylock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play the merchant of the title is Antonio, who borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: Scam involving rent not on

parts.note: a rent is a tear, a rip
off is the opposite of on

explanation.surface: A fraud over rent is simply not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is the noun meaning a tear, not money paid for housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or overcharge is a rip-off, slang synonym.

clue.text: Dr Iannis: a strange person from Mediterranean island

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of Dr Iannis a are made odd by being shuffled

explanation.surface: Dr Iannis is described as an odd islander.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Iannis is the doctor in Captain Corelli's Mandolin, set on a Greek island; a nod to the setter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sardinian is a native of Sardinia, an island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: A little sunshine outside home? Not if this?

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for an adjective: no sunshine if the weather is like this

indicators.note: outside means the beam of sunshine goes around the word for home

parts.note: a ray is a small beam of sunshine
in means at home

explanation.surface: A ray of sunshine outdoors, unless the weather turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather with showers rules out sunshine, so the cryptic hint describes a wet day.

clue.text: Touch nothing removed from hopper

indicators.note: removed from means the letter for nothing is taken out of the word for hopper

parts.note: a toad hops, so it is a hopper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something touches nothing once taken from a hopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch, as in a touch of salt, means a tiny amount, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Doctor keen on eating last of black toast

indicators.note: eating means the word for keen on takes in a letter

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of black is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor who likes eating burnt toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a glass in honour of someone is to toast them, a synonym.

clue.text: Sort of gloves, perhaps, to have on

definitions.meaning: soft goatskin leather used for fine gloves

explanation.surface: Putting on a pair of gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Goatskin gloves are named for the young goat, and to tease someone is to have them on.

clue.text: Queen meeting new street artist from Germany

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: The Queen meets a German artist on a new street.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Surrealist and Dada painter, an example.

clue.text: I had to be listened to and watched

indicators.note: to be listened to signals that the contraction is heard rather than read

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone wanted to be heard and observed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked at someone closely is to have eyed them, a synonym.

clue.text: Permanently in favour of rectitude

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
rectitude is moral goodness, the good

explanation.surface: Someone stands for righteousness forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving for good means leaving for ever, an idiom for permanence.
